close_reason: Landed in b091273 as side-effect of JMAP-t307.1. The medium-fixture docstring in tests/common/mod.rs now says 'base64-encoded filler-block attachment' / 'uniform ASCII filler, not a valid PDF' instead of the prior 'shaped after a small PDF' / 'shaped like a small PDF blob' wording. The Content-Type stays application/pdf because the bead noted that drives attachment classification — the rewrite only fixes the body-content claim. Same correction applies to the bench file's module-level doc comment which now references 'base64 filler-block attachment'.
description:
What is awkward: crate-jmap-mime/benches/mime_pipeline.rs:62-73 docstring says 'base64-encoded attachment shaped after a small PDF' and 'shaped like a small PDF blob'. The actual fixture (line 107) emits 76-char runs of the letter 'A'. There is nothing PDF-shaped about it — no %PDF-1.x header, no xref table, no /Length stream, no octet patterns that would exercise base64 length-quantum behavior differently from any other binary blob.

The MIME adapter under benchmark does not care about content. mime-tree does not validate attachment content. So the 'PDF' claim adds zero benchmarking fidelity and misleads a future reader who sees the docstring and thinks they need to preserve PDF-like structure when editing the fixture.

Suggested rewrite: replace the docstring with a true description — 'base64-encoded filler block (~12 KB encoded) representing a generic binary attachment. Content is uniform ASCII to keep the fixture deterministic across runs.' Drop the application/pdf Content-Type if you do not want to claim PDF semantics; or keep application/pdf because the MIME type drives attachment classification, but stop calling the body PDF-shaped.

This is a small clarity fix, not a benchmarking concern.
title: Medium bench fixture comment claims 'PDF-shaped' but writes filler ASCII
